verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly documents its own background automations within the flag domain. Scheduled flag changes apply targeting changes at future points in time, and progressive and guarded rollouts automatically increase traffic while monitoring metrics for regressions. Adaptive triggers and expiring targets are also listed. These are fixed release-automation primitives, not general-purpose or agent-driven automations an AI-native user can define freely; the MCP server is interactive, driven by an AI client rather than running autonomously. Missing for 10: user-defined general automation/workflow builder, autonomous agent-run background tasks, detail on how triggers work, and independent or hands-on corroboration of unattended operation.
